back: The availability of close substitutes: more substitutes, more elastic demand.

front: How does the share of income spent on a good affect PED?
back: A small share makes demand inelastic; a large share makes it more elastic.

front: Necessities versus luxuries: which has more elastic demand?
back: Luxuries; demand for necessities is inelastic.

front: Effect of habit or addiction on PED?

back: Demand becomes more elastic in the long run as consumers find substitutes.

front: How does the definition of the market affect PED?
back: The narrower the definition (one brand), the more substitutes and the more elastic the demand.

front: Why is demand for one brand more elastic than for the product as a whole?
back: Other brands are close substitutes for one brand, but the product as a whole has no close substitute.
A good that satisfies the same want in a very similar way, so consumers can switch easily.
